$comment: Typed sub-schemas for the agent-facing result contracts. The Rust types in app/core/src/receipt.rs, cut-core::diff, and the comment draft are the source of truth; this file mirrors their serialized shape so an agent and the autopilot can reason over a typed contract instead of prose. A round-trip test in app/core/tests/receipt_schema.rs asserts the Rust types serialize with these required keys, and verbs.json result_schema entries point here.

FixTarget.description: Where a defect lives, lifted from a check's evidence. All optional — a check carries whichever coordinates it measured; never fabricated.

clip_id.description: Clip to target the repair edit.

op_id.description: Op that introduced the defect, when traceable.

FixAction.description: A machine-actionable repair derived from one FAILING check — the contract that the Receipted-Autopilot self-fix loop maps a receipt onto.

check.description: The failing check name this addresses.

fix_verb.description: Verb to call to repair it; '(manual)' when no mechanical fix exists.

fix_args.description: Best-effort partial args for fix_verb; the autopilot merges in render/target context.

measured.description: The measured numbers + target that justify the fix.

rationale.description: One-line why, for the plan + user-facing 'what changed'.

auto_fixable.description: true = mechanical + safe for the self-fix loop; false = needs a human or verify.judge.

CheckResult.description: Result of one verify check. evidence always carries the numbers that justify the verdict (never a bare boolean).

name.description: cut_on_word | lufs | caption_presence | black_or_frozen_frames | silence_at_edges | duration_matches_edl | uniform_border | sources_decodable | cut_on_beat | j_l_cut | footage_profile

details.description: Human-readable structured detail (thresholds, counts, waivers). status:"not_applicable" (with applies_when and reason) = nothing to check on this export, pass stays true; status:"unmeasured" = applies but could not be measured here.

evidence.description: The measured facts behind the verdict (timestamps, LUFS, spans, violations).

RenderReceipt.description: The receipt for a completed render. Persisted at receipts/<render_id>.json, pushed over WS as receipt_ready. 'done requires evidence'.

output_hash.description: Content hash — same input+EDL ⇒ same hash (determinism).

at_op.description: Op id of the log head when the render started — ties the receipt to an exact timeline state.

pass.description: Aggregate: true iff every check passed.

judge.description: Optional perceptual judge (verify.judge) attachment; never a fake pass.

fix_actions.description: One entry per recognised FAILING check — the autopilot self-fix substrate. Empty when every check passed.

encode.description: Which encoder produced the output and whether hardware was asked for and used. Absent on receipts written before this field.

outcome.description: The checks' verdict in one line, each failing check in plain words, and the way forward. Absent on receipts written before this field.

export_checks.description: Every export check with its state for the finished file (checked, found, not checked because an optional tool is missing or the check was not run yet, or an error with its reason). Shape: schema/export-checks.schema.json. Information only: never changes pass, checks or outcome. Absent on receipts written before this field.

CheckOutcome.description: A render's checks in one verdict. problems = the written file is not the timeline (duration_matches_edl or sources_decodable failed); warnings = only quality or editorial checks failed; unmeasured = nothing measured failed but some checks could not run; passed = every check passed. The render job ends with outcome_reason checks_failed for problems and with warnings for warnings.

not_applicable.description: Checks with nothing to check on this export (details.status not_applicable): never a failure or a warning.

EncodeReport.description: The video encoder a render really used. Also returned as `encode` in the render.final job result and in a dry_run plan. render.bundle and render.reframe receipts carry it too: they always encode in software and never ask for hardware, so hardware_requested and hardware_used are both false.

encoder.description: ffmpeg's name for the video encoder that ran, e.g. libx264 or h264_nvenc.

hardware_requested.description: true when the request allowed a hardware encoder (hardware:auto, the default); false for hardware:off.

hardware_used.description: true when the encoder is a hardware encoder.

fallback_reason.description: Present when hardware was requested and software was used: the plain reason and what the person can do about it.

fallback_detail.description: ffmpeg's own error line behind the reason, when there is one.

color.description: What the render did with colour. Absent on receipts written before this field.

memory_note.description: Present when the render used fewer libx264 threads than this computer's automatic count so that it fit the memory free when it started: the plain sentence with both counts and the numbers (the render was slower).

encoder_threads.description: The libx264 thread count of a reduced render (with memory_note), so the same bytes can be made again. Absent at the automatic count.

pipeline.description: Present only when the GPU render path was asked for (SHELLX_CUT_RENDER_GPU): the render path that ran.

pipeline_reason.description: Present when the GPU render path was asked for and the standard path ran: why, in plain words.

ColorReport.description: The colour handling of a render: default exports are SDR BT.709 processed in 8 bits (HDR sources are tone-mapped to SDR); render.final with color:'keep_hdr' writes 10-bit BT.2020 HLG or PQ.

output.description: The delivered picture, e.g. SDR BT.709 or HDR 10-bit HLG (BT.2020).

processing_bit_depth.description: Bits per sample the picture is processed in (8 for SDR, 10 for Keep HDR).

file_bit_depth.description: Bits per sample of the encoded file (10 for ProRes or Keep HDR, else 8).

transfer.description: Output transfer function for Keep HDR renders (arib-std-b67 = HLG, smpte2084 = PQ). Absent for SDR.

hdr10_metadata.description: HDR10 static metadata status (mastering display + MaxCLL/MaxFALL) for Keep HDR renders.

transfer.description: Source transfer as ffprobe names it (arib-std-b67 = HLG, smpte2084 = PQ).

note.description: Plain sentences when a source was converted, reduced in bit depth, graded in SDR, or not converted.

OutputCheckRerunHandle.description: Immediate handle returned by verify.rerun. Poll jobs.status for the separate OutputCheckRerun receipt.

output_hash.description: The source RenderReceipt hash verified before the job was allocated.

OutputCheckRerun.description: Independent persisted output-only recheck receipt. It links to, and never replaces, the RenderReceipt produced by render.final.

source_receipt_id.description: The immutable RenderReceipt.render_id whose output was checked.

verification_receipt.description: Server-generated project-relative path of this separate receipt.

outcome.description: The re-check's verdict in one line, each failing check in plain words, and the way forward.

DiffSummary.description: Result of project.diff — the structural delta between two op-log pointers.

ops.description: Number of ops between the two pointers.

CommentDraft.description: Result of comment.draft — the agent's proposed verb changes for a timecoded review note (not yet applied).
